column1: # ══ Where this table stops, and why ═══════════════════════════════
# 2,913 men are named above. Of the Protestant works in the library,
# 98% now carry a church. What is left unnamed is not a Protestant
# work missing its denomination: it is an Early English Books work
# whose author nobody has placed in any communion at all, so it sits
# outside every tradition and never reaches this facet.
# Those remaining authors are, almost to a man, one printed sheet
# each: a single assize sermon, a single funeral sermon, a single
# pamphlet, by a man with a name, a parish and nothing else. The only
# fact about them is that they printed in English, in England, between
# That fact WOULD support a rule — call them all Church of England and
# be done — and the rule would be right about most of them. It is not
# written here on purpose. Applying it would move some three thousand
# works into Anglican on no evidence, push that one bucket to more
# than half the library, and quietly file every recusant, Quaker and
# Baptist among them under the church they were being fined for
# refusing to attend. A facet that says 98% and shows its working is
# worth more than one that says 100% and cannot.
# So the next pass is not more lines like the last hundred. It is
# evidence: a printer, a parish register, a licensing record, an
# ejection list. Add a line when you have one.
